svg.text: Figure 6.4. The address generator, visit side: one STREAM entry and one counter make each request
v1.0 (spec/machine-spec.md §4.2, §4.5) — the entry comes from figure 6.3's STREAM queue; no per-stream state is kept

g.text: STREAM queue head: this visit's entry (figure 6.3)
Group run: the GROUP queue head is the group (R, t, gap).
For r = 0 … R − 1, each of the t streams gets one visit of 1 cycle
(2 for 128-bit) and pops its STREAM entry; then the group's gap.
Stream run: j = 0, 1, … while send = 1; then gap after; pop.
A visit with send = 1 waits until the SRAM read queue takes its
request; a visit with send = 0 is idle for its visit time.
e (18 bits): r in a group run, j in a stream run
send: in a stream run, send = 0 ends the stream
taken: the visit is done; the timetable moves on
token, pushed when the request is taken
dst (6), mode (3, zero-extended to 4), addr (12: the word, or 0), two packets (1: z = 2)
read return: the element (32, 64 or 128 bits), in request order
The increments: element e of a stream, for each read size (source s, cm field c)
• Nothing per stream is stored: each visit's address, dst and word come from its STREAM entry and the one counter, and the counters, the request and the token FIFO are the only state.

• The z = 2 packets: one request reads the 128-bit element from one row, or from two when the element crosses a row boundary; the packet builder sends it as two packets on consecutive cycles, low half then

• A spanning read (any element that crosses a row boundary) costs a second row access (row + 1, possibly in the next area; figure 7.2). In a group run it costs a cycle and sets drift (TILE_CONDITIONS bit 0,
§4.1), so a group run's streams are laid out to avoid it.
• A 32-bit element goes in the payload's low half with the high half 0 (§4.2). Read size 00 is an error even at count 0. A group's streams share one read size.
• A visit whose STREAM entry is not in the queue yet waits the same on every tile: part of the timetable, not lateness; with ag_lookahead at its bound it doesn't happen.
• A request the SRAM read queue does not take holds the visit until it is taken. In a group run that sets the drift condition (TILE_CONDITIONS bit 0, §4.13): the tile has fallen behind its timetable.
count, d, mode, size, gap after, source, cm field
the element (j or r); offer this cycle (a 128-bit visit takes 2 cycles)
chunk = source + (e << z); dst = (me + d) mod 64; mode; width (one request per element)
mode 5: cm + 2e (32, 64 bits) or cm + 4e (128: the builder adds 2 for the second packet); else 0
SRAM read queue and its return
junction (lines that cross without a dot don't connect)

svg.text: Each visit takes one STREAM entry and the counter e (the rotation r, or the element j): it sends element e if e < count, from source + (e << z),
so the source steps by 1, 2 or 4 chunks per element for 32-, 64- or 128-bit reads. The token carries dst, mode and the mode-5 word to the packets.
